title: Quadratic prefix values from consistency checks
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a Boolean sequence of length $n$, and let a Boolean table assign values to the linear prefixes, quadratic prefixes, and coordinate products. Suppose the linear prefix at $0$ and quadratic prefix at $0$ are false, the quadratic prefix at $n$ is true, and for every $i<n$ the linear prefix at $i+1$ is the sum in $\mathbb F_2$ of the linear prefix at $i$ and the image of $w_i$; the product entry at $i$ is the conjunction of the linear prefix at $i$ and $w_i$; and the quadratic prefix at $i+1$ is the sum in $\mathbb F_2$ of the quadratic prefix at $i$ and the image of that product entry. Then for every $k\le n$, the image in $\mathbb F_2$ of the table's quadratic prefix at $k$ equals the quadratic value of the first $k$ mapped coordinates of $w$.
hypotheses_covered: $w$ is a Boolean sequence indexed by $0,\ldots,n-1$
the proof table is Boolean-valued on the specified prefix and product indices
all endpoint and transition checks hold
$k$ is an integer with $0\le k\le n$
